name: How does the timeline for a kitchen addition compare to an interior kitchen remodel?

mainEntity.name: How does the timeline for a kitchen addition compare to an interior kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen addition usually takes longer than a standard interior remodel because it includes exterior excavation, concrete curing, weather-tight framing, and exterior siding or roofing. While an interior kitchen update might take several weeks to a few months, building an exterior room addition typically spans several months from site preparation to final walk-through. Factors that influence the timeline include local permit approval speeds, site access for excavation machinery, weather conditions during foundation and framing stages, and lead times on custom-ordered items like cabinetry, windows, and exterior materials.
acceptedAnswer.description: Kitchen additions take longer because they require site excavation, foundation pouring, framing, exterior weatherproofing, and final interior finishing.
